title: Passivity Correction of the Thermistor Model in Bolometric Power Sensors and Its Dependence on Bead Temperature
abstract: This paper closes a series of works on thermistor bolometric power sensors, coaxial and waveguide, by treating what the two have in common. The per-state transformation m introduced in the waveguide work, which corrects the thermistor impedances of the model in each bridge state so that the two-port of the mount is passive, is analyzed on the eleven sensors of the preceding papers: the corrections are a few tenths of a percent in the coaxial mounts and one to two percent in the waveguide mounts, follow one pattern within each family, and the hottest state is the one whose efficiency departs most from the others. The transformation is tested by an independent measurement: the substituted powers of the three states, read with the manufacturer's procedure against a leveled source whose reflection is obtained from the closure of three Apollonius circles, give efficiency ratios of 0.999 +/- 0.016 and 0.997 +/- 0.008 (k = 2), which contain the values at the passivity floor (0.996, 0.998) and exclude those of the first pass (0.941, 1.023). Three sensors were swept in the bridge resistance, 23 and 31 states, and a fourth is treated apart: the correction reduces to one constant per state, the parallel resistance of the bead, represented by a law with one term scaling with the bridge resistance and one exponential in the bead temperature, with one thermal coefficient per family. The same property explains why the cross-ratio of four measured reflection coefficients, invariant under any state-independent two-port, departs from that of the four bridge resistances.
